subject: Meteorology
title: Global vs. Regional Models
description: A quick win: understand Global vs. Regional Models.

hook.text: Global models cover the whole Earth but with coarse resolution—regional models zoom in on smaller areas.

buildup.text: The GFS (US) and ECMWF (European) are the two leading global models—each with grid spacing of about 9–13 km.

discovery.text: Regional models like the HRRR run at 3 km or finer—resolving individual thunderstorms that globals miss.

twist.text: Regional models need boundary conditions from global models—they can't exist alone without the bigger picture.

climax.text: ECMWF has led global accuracy for decades—but the GFS and others are closing the gap with each upgrade.

punchline.text: Global sets the stage—regional fills in the details.
